newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher, fuelled by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher, fuelled by blue chips.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Wednesday, fuelled by strong gains in blue chips.
"It was a good day, but still somewhat boring," a trader said. "There was not much to trade on. The market opened strongly, but got tired towards the end when the U.S. opened lower."
The exchange's general index rose 0.89 percent to 2,730.86 in turnover of 4.79 billion crowns.
Automotive group Volvo stole centre stage, rising 8.5 crowns to a record close of 205.5 on a stronger dollar and a positive car sales forecast from Sweden's HUI.

"There is a lot speaking in favour of Volvo in the shortterm," a trader said. "Partly HUI figures with a expectations of strong car sales, partly a strong dollar and partly the company's planned share redemption."
Drugs major Astra and telecoms group Ericsson benefited from investors turning to heavyweights. Astra rose 4.5 to 360 and Ericsson gained three to 263.5.
Banks performed poorly, however, with the sector index slipping 0.12 percent on profit taking. Handelsbanken dropped three to 226.5.
